rules: Pure price/volume products need no fundamental leg: CS_ZSCORE/CS_DEMEAN of a range-or-displacement leg ($high-$low, TS_DELTA($open,w), TS_STD($open,w)) times CS_ZSCORE/TS_RANK of a volume or $dollar_volume leg took 5 of 9 accepts and the round's top 3 fitnesses (4.592, 3.613, 3.338). Keep mining this pairing across windows and field pairs.

42% of rejects (8/19) were in-round duplicates, clustered on TS_MIN($low,21) range/position ratios and $asset_turnover/$earnings_per_share crossed with TS_MEAN or TS_STD($return). Dedupe every new proposal against everything already queued this round, not just the archive.

A kernel that fails cheap_screen bare can pass once crossed with an unused fundamental rank: ($dollar_volume/$volume)/$open failed alone (|t| 0.54) but hit 0.947 once multiplied by CS_RANK($operating_margin). Retry marginal bare rejects with a fresh fundamental multiplier instead of discarding them.

Swapping the price field in an accepted shape does not decorrelate: $adj_close vs $close in a book_per_share ratio hit rho 1.000, and $close vs $open inside a TS_DELTA(...,5) spread leg hit 0.839. Vary the operator or window, not which of open/high/low/close/adj_close fills a slot.

Raw-$return kernels without a fundamental partner stayed weak: SIGN($return) x CS_RANK($volume) and COUNT($volume>DELAY($volume,1),10) x CS_RANK($return) both failed cheap_screen. COUNT-style and sign-style kernels need a fundamental rank on the other leg to clear screen, as already proven for $roa.

CS_RANK(TS_STD($return,5)) and CS_ZSCORE(TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21)) are now saturated as standalone fragments, each triggering an archive_subtree reject regardless of the paired leg. Don't reuse either verbatim even with a new partner.

This round's accepts skewed heavily to price_volume niches (7 of 9); only one touched a fundamental (operating_margin, landing in slow/mixed/high). If broader fundamental/mixed niche coverage matters, prioritize fundamental-crossed proposals next round before price_volume slots fill further.

MIN($return,0) (raw downside truncation, no fundamental) missed cheap_screen at |t| 0.99, right at the threshold. Unlike EPS downside truncation which is productive, truncating raw $return alone is unproven; pair with a fundamental rather than resubmitting bare.
